title: Efficient Key Recovery from Massive Superpolies
summary: Disjoint sets exploiting sparse superpolies improve cube attacks but require huge memory; efficient key recovery from increasingly massive full-key superpolies remains open.

formal_statement.body: In cube attacks, a disjoint-set key-recovery method can exploit sparse variables in a superpoly to improve attacks, but it incurs huge memory cost. Since superpolies are expected to become increasingly massive as the number of rounds grows, develop an efficient secret-key recovery method for cube attacks based on massive superpolies involving all secret-key bits while addressing the disjoint-set method's memory bottleneck.

scope.domain: Cube-attack key recovery using massive superpolies involving all secret-key bits.
parameters: Number of rounds: expected to drive growth in superpoly size
scope.unresolved_remainder: Develop an efficient secret-key recovery method for massive full-key superpolies that overcomes the disjoint-set method's memory bottleneck.

citations.label: Massive Superpoly Recovery with Nested Monomial Predictions

progress.summary: The paper reports improved key-recovery attacks using sparse superpoly structure and a disjoint-set method, while identifying the method's huge memory cost. It explicitly poses efficient recovery from increasingly massive full-key superpolies as an open question.
citation_labels: Kai Hu et al., Massive Superpoly Recovery with Nested Monomial Predictions
